x: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947. 26 November 1949 is when the Constitution (with its Preamble) was adopted, and 1976 is the 42nd Amendment.
t: Separate moving (13 Dec 1946) from adopting (22 Jan 1947).

x: Sovereign – supreme authority, free from external control; Socialist – reducing inequality; Republic – elected head of State; Fraternity – dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the Nation.
t: Match each Preamble word to its meaning.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the LIC of India case (1995) reaffirmed what Kesavananda Bharati (1973) settled — that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
t: Check whether the case in R is authority for A.

x: C is incorrect: the Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced in court. The rest are right: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist, Secular and Integrity — the only amendment so far — and Berubari (1960) held it was not part of the Constitution.
t: Remember the Preamble guides but is not enforceable.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the Preamble's date is 26 November 1949, 'Federal' is not in it, and it can be amended under Article 368. III is wrong: the Preamble neither confers powers nor creates rights.
t: The Preamble is neither a source of power nor of rights.

x: Both are true: the idea of a Preamble came from the US Constitution, while its language was influenced by the Australian Constitution.
t: Separate the idea (USA) from the language (Australia).

x: Berubari (1960), Golaknath (1967), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), LIC of India (1995): C, D, A, B.
t: Order the Preamble cases by year.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable under Article 368, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed.
t: Check whether R is the ruling that sets the rule in A.

x: All three are correct: the people resolved to make India a Sovereign State, and the Preamble calls it Democratic and a Republic (with Socialist and Secular added in 1976).
t: Recall the five words describing India in the Preamble.

x: Justice – social, economic and political; Liberty – of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; Equality – of status and opportunity; Fraternity – to be promoted among all citizens.
t: Match each ideal to the phrase that follows it in the Preamble.

x: All four are correct: secularism in India means equal respect for all religions, and democracy is government of, by and for the people.
t: Check each definition against its concept.

x: Both are true: the Preamble says the people 'adopt, enact and give to ourselves' the Constitution on 26 November 1949.
t: Recall the three verbs of the Preamble's last line.

x: A republic has an elected head of State, not a hereditary one. Options B and C describe monarchy, and D contradicts sovereignty.
All three are correct: justice is social, economic and political; liberty is of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality is of status and opportunity.
t: Recall the qualifiers of each Preamble ideal.

x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution, overruling Berubari (1960), which had said it was not; LIC of India (1995) reaffirmed this. Golaknath (1967) dealt with amending Fundamental Rights.
t: Link 'Preamble is part of the Constitution' to the basic-structure case.

x: Both are true: the Preamble is called the key to the Constitution and its soul.
t: Recall the descriptions given to the Preamble.

x: K.M. Munshi called the Preamble the 'Political Horoscope' of the Constitution. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul', and Hidayatullah called the Preamble its soul.
t: Match each description to the person who gave it.

x: All three are correct: the Preamble reflects the philosophy, ideals and objectives of the Constitution.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the 'Mini Constitution' because of its sweeping changes. 'Soul' and 'key' describe the Preamble and 'political horoscope' is Munshi's phrase for it.
t: Separate the 42nd Amendment's nickname from the Preamble's.
